components.cost_effect: One center jet constructs the model; evaluating the certificate costs at most one further unknown-operator query.
components.goal: Produce a feasible model point and a genuine original-domain normal from one returned jet.
components.key_estimate: E=G(y)-Gbar_x(y) obeys ||E||<=Lp||y-x||^p/p!. The model is uniquely solvable on admissible jets; source Lemmas 4.1–4.2 establish continuous selection on the admissible closed set, extended by a fixed feasible point elsewhere without a certificate.
components.name: Exact regularized Taylor-model VI
components.operation: At x form Gbar_x using derivatives through p-1; solve equation (4.1) with beta=2Lp/(p-1)!; set n=-Gbar_x(y)-beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x).
components.requires: The stated regularity, monotonicity, Lp>0 and known compact convex X; exact model computation convention.
transfer_checks: An approximate model solve requires new error accounting and a genuine normal construction.
Do not replace X by an artificial localization ball and retain the same normal claim.

components.cost_effect: At most two original queries, including certificate evaluation; normal membership is independent of the radius promise.
components.goal: Convert a valid distance radius into an actual normal certificate.
components.key_estimate: A_p=(2p+1)3^p/p!; ||y-x||<=3r and ||G(y)+n||<=A_p Lp r^p. A complete argument is included in thm.arxiv2609_13462.base_trial_certificate.
components.name: Evaluated model correction
components.operation: Use the same full model at x, retain its normal n, and evaluate G(y); return (y,n,G(y)).
components.requires: A VI solution z_star with ||x-z_star||<=r; monotonicity suffices for this component.
transfer_checks: The radius bound is needed for the residual estimate, not for normal membership.
Acceptance requires the evaluated norm test.

limitations.statement: A false radius still gives a finite feasible schedule, but does not establish distance halving. A weighted average is not supplied with a residual certificate.
Exact information complexity does not imply efficient numerical model solving or a bit-complexity bound.

performance_links.scope_note: Proposition 4.5: valid radius, strong monotonicity, distance output and <=2T original queries.

variants.cost: At most 2T unknown-G feasible order-p queries: one center jet and one evaluation at y per nonzero step; the exact-solution branch needs only its center jet. Exact model solving, projections, arithmetic and aggregation are internal information-model operations; no polynomial arithmetic or bit-cost bound is supplied. For a known affine regularization G(u)=F(u)+a u+b, a G-jet is simulated by one original-F jet: value adds a u+b, Jacobian adds aI, higher derivatives are unchanged. Thus the same <=2T bound charges original-F queries, including evaluations.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Section 3.2 pp.8–9; Section 4 pp.11–14; Algorithm 1 p.15.
variants.name: Halve(G,w,mu,r)
variants.output: Early exact solution y, otherwise s_avg/Lambda in X. Under the valid distance promise, distance to z_star is <=r/2. No tangent-residual bound is asserted for the final average.
public_inputs: Known nonempty compact convex X subset R^d, d>=1, diam(X)<=D with D>0
w in X; fixed integer p>=2; known Lp>0; mu>0; r>0
variants.query_and_update: For i=0,...,T-1: query the full jet at x; form Gbar_x(y)=sum_{j=0}^{p-1}(1/j!)D^jG(x)[y-x]^j with D^0G=G; solve exactly 0 in Gbar_x(y)+beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x)+N_X(y). If y=x, return y, an exact VI solution. Otherwise query G(y); set lambda=(beta||y-x||^(p-1))^(-1); s_avg=s_avg+lambda y; Lambda=Lambda+lambda; x=Pi_X(x-lambda G(y)). The model also gives n=-Gbar_x(y)-beta||y-x||^(p-1)(y-x) in N_X(y).
variants.requirements: Euclidean vector norm and induced multilinear operator norm. G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X; ||D^(p-1)G(u)-D^(p-1)G(v)||op<=Lp||u-v|| and <G(u)-G(v),u-v>>=mu||u-v||^2 on X. No separate lower-derivative or operator-value bound is required. The unique VI solution satisfies 0 in G(z_star)+N_X(z_star), where N_X(y)={n:<n,u-y><=0 for every u in X}. All operations use the original known domain X.
variants.state_and_initialization: x=w; Lambda=0; s_avg=0; b_p=2p/p!; beta=b_p Lp=2Lp/(p-1)!; T=max{1,ceil([2b_p(4/3)^((p-1)/2)Lp r^(p-1)/mu]^(2/(p+1)))}. The hidden solution z_star and actual distance are not inputs; ||w-z_star||<=r is a promise used only for the guarantee.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use precisely the finite T above, equation (4.11); only the y=x branch stops early. The model solve and projection are exact internal operations on returned coefficients and the known domain, not free calls to a resolvent of unknown G.

summary: A deterministic exact-information routine that halves a valid distance bound for a strongly monotone VI in at most 2T_p original-oracle queries. Its weighted average has a distance guarantee, not a claimed tangent-residual guarantee.
title: Halve: finite tensor-extragradient distance halving
use_when: A strongly monotone VI has a supplied valid distance radius and exact feasible jets.
Use BaseTrial instead when an evaluated normal certificate is required.
